topic: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
usual_baseline: Surgery within 36 hours in 39.6–48.3% [1271, 1315]; best practice tariff met in 28–44.4% [1315, 1306]. Orthogeriatric input is often weak: 35% [1232], 11% geriatrician assessment [1552], mean 91 hours to review [1323]. Preoperative medical assessment 19% [1323]. Delays are mostly medical, then theatre space [1232, 1267].
fix_that_works: Whole-pathway redesign with orthogeriatricians: within 36 hours 39.6% to 84%, tariff 28% to 83%, 30-day mortality 7.8% to 5.3% [1315]. Joint admission pathway: orthogeriatric review 91 to 19 hours, mortality 14% to 4% [1323]. Clerking booklet and orthogeriatric rounds: tariff 44.4% to 91.7% [1306]. Tariff measures: 48.3% to 73.4% [1271]. National database: geriatrician assessment 11% to 86% [1552].
fix_that_fails: Stopping continuous audit lost gains: surgery within 48 hours fell from 98.4% to 91.8% [1299]. Nationally, tariff compliance reached only 21% and time to surgery stayed hardest [1552]. Benchmarking lifted nerve blocks only to 25.4% [1484]. Circulating results did not change 3-month function or mortality [1194]. ED booklet section complete in 74.1% [1306].
consultant_advice: Auditing your unit against the tariff repeats what the national database already reports. Use its data rather than collecting your own. More useful: find why your patients breach, such as medical optimisation or theatre space, and audit the fix. Keep measuring after the change; gains fade when audit stops [1299].
